items.title: The dual-canonical, canonical and quasi-canonical Fock bases
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked quantum based/global lattice and normalized quasi-$R$ suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]: the
**source parameter** is $s$, the **library parameter** is $t=s^{-1}$, the
monomial basis of the Fock module is $\{M_A\}$, and $\psi$ is the ordinary
compatible bar of
[[thm-the-qg-tensor-product-bar-is-triangular-and-compatible-with-fock-truncations]],
which is triangular and integral on the monomial basis.

The **source dual-canonical family** $(L_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family
with
$$L_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s\,\mathbb Z[s]\,M_B,$$
and the **canonical family** $(T_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family with
$$T_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]\,M_B .$$

Let $d_{A,B}(s)$ and $p_{A,B}(-s)$ be the transition coefficients defined by
$$M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}(s)\,L_A,\qquad L_B=\sum_A p_{A,B}(-s)\,M_A,$$
and define the **quasi-canonical family** by
$$P_A:=\sum_B d_{A,B}(s)\,M_B,\qquad\text{so that}\qquad M_A=\sum_B p_{A,B}(-s)\,P_B .$$
The families $L$ and $T$ are ordinary-bar fixed; $P$ generally is not.

The **reverse-factor monomials** $\widetilde M_A$ use the reverse-column
reading of the tableau $A$; the corresponding bar-fixed families
$\widetilde L_A,\widetilde T_A$ are defined by the same triangular conditions
with respect to $\widetilde M_A$, so that $\widetilde L_A$ is supported on
$B>A$. **Rectification** is the weight-preserving combinatorial identification
of the original lower ground component $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$ with the
reverse-factor lower ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, given by reading
down columns and reverse row insertion.

The **source sesquilinear form** is the $\mathbb C$-antilinear-in-the-first
argument pairing with
$$\langle M_A,\psi M_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},$$
and the **bilinear reverse-factor form** is
$$C(\widetilde M_A,\psi M_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$
Thus the labelled monomial Gram matrices of the two forms are the inverse
ordinary-bar matrix, not the identity. Transition duality gives
$$\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$

All four families are Laurent-integral bases of the finite Fock cuts and
commute with the upper-cut and common-bottom-tail embeddings. On a highest
constituent, the source bilinear normalization $C_0$ and the library
polarization of [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]] differ by
an explicit weight power, proved in the global-basis comparison later in this
pair; no unqualified library-upper/ordinary-bar identification is asserted.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked quantum suppliers. A finite cut of the Fock module with its monomial basis $\{M_A\}$, the ordinary compatible bar $\psi$ with $\psi M_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]M_B$, the reverse-column reading and rectification, and the two forms of the Definition.

[F1] Fock bar and monomial basis ([[thm-the-qg-tensor-product-bar-is-triangular-and-compatible-with-fock-truncations]], [[thm-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module-has-the-column-monomial-basis]], [[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]): $\psi$ is involutive, triangular with coefficients in $\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]$, preserves the integral monomial lattice, and commutes with the cut embeddings; the monomials form a Laurent-integral basis.

[F2] Global bases in the library ([[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]], [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]]): existence, bar invariance and uniqueness of the lower global basis, the form-dual upper basis, and the bar lattice/based-module framework.

[F3] Normalized finite quasi-$R$ intertwiner ([[thm-the-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiner-exists-and-is-unique]], [[lem-quasi-r-intertwining-determines-the-inverse-and-coproduct-factorizations]]): the positive-first/negative-second family is uniquely determined by $\Theta_0=1$ and $\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\overline\Delta(u)$, with $\overline\Delta(u)=(\bar{\phantom{x}}\otimes\bar{\phantom{x}})\Delta(\bar u)$, and its finite-cut evaluations are the tensor bars of [F1].

## Verification

1.1 **The two triangular charts.** Fix a total order refining the finite-cut Bruhat order. Construct a fixed vector with leading term $M_A$ by descending elimination on its lower support. Suppose its bar discrepancy has largest remaining term $rM_B$; involutivity gives $r+\bar r=0$, since every higher discrepancy has already vanished. Write $r=\sum_{n>0}r_n(s^n-s^{-n})$. There is a unique $c_+=\sum_{n>0}r_ns^n$ in $s\mathbb Z[s]$ with $c_+-\bar c_+=r$, and a unique $c_-=-\sum_{n>0}r_ns^{-n}$ in $s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]$ with the same property. Adding the relevant $c_\pm M_B$ removes this discrepancy and changes only smaller ones. Finite descending elimination constructs the two charts, with uniqueness by the same largest-coefficient argument. This explicitly retains conjugation in the fixed-vector equation $c=B_\psi\bar c$. Each chart is integral unitriangular, hence an integral basis. [F1, algebra]

1.2 **Rectification of the ground components.** On a column cancel the simultaneous $i,i+1$ occurrences; concatenate the column words and cancel $-+$ pairs. In reverse tensor order this is the lower rule with ordinary column reading. Weakly increasing rows are stable: a changed entry violating the neighboring row inequality would have an equal neighboring entry giving a later surviving $+$ or earlier surviving $-$, contrary to the selected extremum; if that neighboring sign is cancelled, column strictness gives its matching mate in the same intervening strip and cancels the selected sign too. Apply this matching successively across neighboring columns, including unequal heights. The only highest tableau in this closed set is ground: starting at the rightmost column, absence of unmatched minus forces consecutive bottom entries from the alphabet minimum; induct leftward using row inequalities on the overlap, while a gap above it gives an unmatched minus with no right-hand mate. Raising decreases the entry sum to its finite lower bound, so the whole closed standard set is the reverse lower ground component. For the original lower order read columns from the right and align their tops; the same argument gives the reverse-standard set. Insert its reverse-column word by bumping the smallest larger entry. Adjacent insertions differ by the Knuth moves $acb\leftrightarrow cab$ for $a\le b<c$ and $bac\leftrightarrow bca$ for $a<b\le c$. Cancelling the three-letter signatures for each adjacent alphabet pair preserves their unmatched counts and selected sign, and the changed entry follows its bump path, so insertion commutes with crystal edges. Reverse insertion, bumping the largest smaller entry in the backward column word, reverses each successive bump path and preserves the row and column inequalities. Thus the two procedures are inverse, weight preserving, send ground to ground and identify $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$ with $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ in the asserted lower charts. [F1, algebra]

1.3 **The Gram matrices.** Put $B=B_\psi$ with $\psi M_j=\sum_i B_{ij}M_i$, and write $S_{ij}=\langle M_i,M_j\rangle$. The normalization $\langle M_i,\psi M_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}$ says $SB=I$, since the second argument is linear. Therefore $S=B^{-1}$, with no transpose. Exactly the same equation holds for $C(\widetilde M_i,M_j)$, since its second argument is also linear, so its matrix is again $B^{-1}$. Involutivity says $B\bar B=I$, hence $B^{-1}=\bar B$. [F1, algebra]

2.1 **The quasi-canonical family and the inverse charts.** Let $U$ be the coefficient matrix of $L$ in $M$, with columns labelled by vectors, and set $D=U^{-1}$. The coefficient of $L_A$ in $M_B$ is $D_{A,B}=d_{A,B}(s)$, while $U_{A,B}=p_{A,B}(-s)$. The coefficient matrix of $P$ is $D^{\mathsf T}$, whose inverse is $U^{\mathsf T}$. These identities prove both displayed quasi-canonical expansions with the stated index positions and show integrality. The fixed-chart equation is $B_\psi\bar U=U$, where coefficient conjugation sends $s$ to $s^{-1}$. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 **Cuts and integrality.** All four families are computed weight by weight from the same triangular equations, so they are Laurent-integral bases of each finite cut. Since the embeddings of [F1] preserve the monomial basis and the bar, they preserve these equations and hence the four families; on the highest constituent the normalized source pairing is $C_0$ up to the explicit weight rescaling proved in the global-basis comparison. [F1, step 1.1, step 1.2]



2.3 **The reverse-bar adjoint calculation.** Let $\omega$ be the linear anti-automorphism $E_i\mapsto F_i$, $F_i\mapsto E_i$, $D_a\mapsto D_a$; reversing products preserves the toral mixed, commutator and Serre relations. Write $H_i=D_iD_{i+1}^{-1}$. The source coproduct has $\Delta E_i=1\otimes E_i+E_i\otimes H_i$, $\Delta F_i=F_i\otimes1+H_i^{-1}\otimes F_i$. Put $\mathscr A=\mathrm{flip}\circ(\omega\otimes\omega)$. Direct substitution gives $\mathscr A\Delta E_i=F_i\otimes1+H_i\otimes F_i=\overline\Delta F_i$ and $\mathscr A\Delta F_i=1\otimes E_i+E_i\otimes H_i^{-1}=\overline\Delta E_i$; the toral coproduct is unchanged. Hence $\mathscr A\Delta(u)=\overline\Delta(\omega u)$ and $\mathscr A\overline\Delta(u)=\Delta(\omega u)$ on the generated algebra. Applying the anti-automorphism $\mathscr A$ to $\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\overline\Delta(u)$ gives $\mathscr A(\Theta)\overline\Delta(\omega u)=\Delta(\omega u)\mathscr A(\Theta)$. Its degree-zero term is one and flip with $E/F$ exchange preserves the positive-first/negative-second completion. The exact normalized uniqueness of [F3] therefore gives $\mathscr A(\Theta)=\Theta$. On each ordered minuscule wedge factor the $E_i,F_i$ matrices are mutually transpose and the $D_a$ matrices are diagonal, so transpose realizes $\omega$. Consequently transposing the original two-factor bar and reversing factors gives the reverse-factor bar in the same tableau labelling. The same statement for successive prefixes follows from the coproduct factorization and parenthesization independence of [F1], [F3]; thus $\widetilde B=B^{\mathsf T}$. In raw full-tensor labels this also reads $(\widetilde E_i)^{\mathsf T}=\overline{F_i}$, $(\widetilde F_i)^{\mathsf T}=\overline{E_i}$, where the bar acts on matrix coefficients and conjugates all toral weight powers. Finally $\widetilde B^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}B=B=\overline{B^{-1}}$, so $C(\widetilde\psi x,\psi y)=\overline{C(x,y)}$. This adjoint calculation uses the two ordinary tensor bars independently of charge transpose. [F1, F3, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 **The sesquilinear delta identity.** By step 2.1 the coefficient matrices are $U$ for $L$ and $D^{\mathsf T}$ for $P$, with $D=U^{-1}$. Thus the pairing matrix is $\overline{D^{\mathsf T}}^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}U=\bar D B^{-1}U$. The fixed-chart equation $B\bar U=U$ gives $B^{-1}U=\bar U$, so this product is $\bar D\bar U=I$. This proves $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$ directly, including coefficient conjugation. [step 2.1, step 1.3, algebra]



3.2 **The reverse-factor delta identities.** Let $\widetilde U$ and $V$ be the coefficient matrices of $\widetilde L$ and $T$. Since $B\bar V=V$, their pairing matrix is $\widetilde U^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}V=\widetilde U^{\mathsf T}\bar V$. Both $\widetilde U-I$ and $\bar V-I$ have coefficients in $s\mathbb Z[s]$, so this matrix lies in $I+s\operatorname{Mat}(\mathbb Z[s])$. Step 2.3 makes each entry bar fixed, because the vectors being paired are fixed. The only bar-fixed polynomial in $s\mathbb Z[s]$ is zero, proving $C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB}$. Replacing the positive charts by $\widetilde T$ and $L$ gives a matrix in $I+s^{-1}\operatorname{Mat}(\mathbb Z[s^{-1}])$ and the same bar argument, proving $C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}$. [step 1.1, step 1.3, step 2.3, algebra]

4.1 **Conclusion.** The four families $L,T,P$ and their reverse-factor counterparts are well-defined Laurent-integral bases of the finite Fock cuts with the stated triangular charts and delta pairings, and the reverse ground component is identified with $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ by rectification. All later comparisons with the library upper family use the explicit weight rescaling of the global-basis theorem, never the bare names of the families. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 1.3, step 3.1, step 2.3, step 3.2] ∎

items.title: Type-A tableau central summands are single linkage blocks
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For the Fock shape
$n_1\ge\cdots\ge n_l$ (the original nonincreasing-charge hypothesis) and any
admitted integral entry multiset, the genuine $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ parabolic
central summand labelled by its strict-column tableaux is a **single linkage
block**. The same holds for its reverse-column/reversed-Levi counterpart.
This includes repeated-entry singular ambient characters. The proof uses
actual indecomposable generalized standards and locally constructed tiltings:
adjacent-column positive exclusive-pair canonical coefficients specialize
to $1$, so those labels lie in a common actual linkage block, and these edges
connect the whole fixed-margin binary tableau fiber. No future
higher-Schur/cyclotomic-centre theorem is imported.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A finite genuine $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ parabolic central summand as in [[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]], with its actual generalized standards $\Delta_B$, simples $L_A$ and projective covers; the reversed-block construction and its contravariant/covariant equivalences $\Psi,F$ of [[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]; the Fock tableaux and their monomials of [[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]; and the four Fock bases and forms of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]].

[F1] Highest-weight structure and filtered categories ([[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]], [[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]]): finite $\Delta$-flags, the homological criterion $\mathcal F(\Delta)=\{N:\operatorname{Ext}^1(N,\nabla_A)=0\ \forall A\}$, uniqueness of indecomposable tilting objects with a given bottom label, BGG reciprocity $[P_A:\Delta_B]=[\Delta_B:L_A]$, and restricted duality.

[F2] Semi-regular duality ([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]): $\Psi(\bar\Delta(A))\cong\Delta(A)$, $F=D\Psi$ sends opposite standards to target costandards, and both preserve the central blocks and reverse the label order.

[F3] Singular/parabolic coefficients ([[thm-singular-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]], [[thm-weyl-character-formula]]): the ordinary spherical values $P_{yw_0,ww_0}(1)$ compute the singular multiplicities, and the finite Weyl character formula gives the signed Levi expansion of characters.

[F4] Fock bases and forms ([[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]]): the monomial basis $M_A$, the source dual-canonical and canonical families $L,T$, the complementary triangular charts $d,p$, the source bilinear form $C$ with $C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}$ and $C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB}$, and the bar triangularity $T_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]M_B$.

[F5] Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The actual normalized projective image.** Fix one finite highest-weight central summand and a label $B$, and put $X(B)=\Psi(P^{\bar p}(B))$. The source projective has its highest-weight exact sequence $0\to\bar K(B)\to P^{\bar p}(B)\to\bar\Delta(B)\to0$, with a finite standard flag on $\bar K(B)$ using strictly higher source labels. Exact contravariance of $\Psi$ gives $0\to\Delta(B)\to X(B)\to\Psi\bar K(B)\to0$. Order reversal makes the quotient standard-filtered by labels strictly below $B$. Thus this is an actual normalized bottom inclusion, and $\Delta(B)$ occurs once. The endomorphism ring of $X(B)$ is opposite to the local ring of its source projective cover, so $X(B)$ is indecomposable. [F1, F2, F5]

1.2 **The CWZ parameter, coproduct and ordered labels.** In the two-wedge convention of Cheng–Wang–Zhang, write $q$ for their parameter and $K_a$ for their toral generator. The exact transport to [F4] is $q\mapsto s^{-1}$, $K_a\mapsto D_a^{-1}$, $E_a\mapsto E_a$, $F_a\mapsto F_a$, and $K_f\mapsto M_f$ for the same two decreasing columns in the same left/right order. Their natural eigenvalue $q^{\delta_{ab}}$ becomes $s^{-\delta_{ab}}$, the eigenvalue of $D_a^{-1}$. The toral relations and the $E/F$ commutator agree because both numerator and denominator of the toral fraction reverse sign. Their coproducts are $\Delta E_a=1\otimes E_a+E_a\otimes K_{a+1}K_a^{-1}$ and $\Delta F_a=F_a\otimes1+K_aK_{a+1}^{-1}\otimes F_a$; these become exactly $1\otimes E_a+E_a\otimes D_aD_{a+1}^{-1}$ and $F_a\otimes1+D_a^{-1}D_{a+1}\otimes F_a$ of [F4]. Thus reciprocal parameter substitution alone is accompanied by toral inversion, and no reversal of tensor factors or tableau entries is used. The quantum Serre coefficients are unchanged under reciprocation, and the two bars agree on coefficients and generators: both fix $E_a,F_a$ and invert the torus. The displayed source coproduct and ordered factor actions are those of [[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]. The ordered wedge basis has coefficient-one adjacent-entry replacement actions, so it identifies the elementary wedge factors; their relation on unordered wedges becomes $-s$, consistently with this transport. A swap of exclusive left $b>$ right $a$ gives a strictly smaller label in both orders, since the left prefix changes by the positive root $\delta_a-\delta_b$. Consequently the CWZ positive-$q$ triangular chart maps to the negative-$s^{-1}$ chart of $T$, not to the positive-$s$ chart of $L$. [F4, algebra]

2.1 **Tilting and an actual normalized dual flag.** For an extension $0\to X(B)\to Z\to\Delta(A)\to0$, the middle object is standard-filtered by extension closure. Inverting $\Psi$ turns it into an extension with the opposite projective as quotient, which splits. Hence $\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta(A),X(B))=0$ for every $A$, and the criterion of [F1] makes $X(B)$ costandard-filtered and therefore tilting. The object $DX(B)$ is also tilting and indecomposable; duality fixes simple classes, so all its composition labels are $\le B$ and $[DX(B):L(B)]=1$. In the lower highest-weight ideal of labels $\le B$, $\Delta(B)$ is the maximal-labelled projective. The maximal standard trace proved in [[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]] injects $\Delta(B)$ into the standard-filtered $DX(B)$ with quotient standard-filtered by strictly smaller labels: its multiplicity space has dimension $[DX(B):L(B)]=1$. Thus the dual has an actual normalized bottom-standard sequence. Uniqueness of such indecomposable tiltings in [F1] gives $X(B)\cong DX(B)$. This normalization uses the proved maximal trace and does not follow from exchanging the kinds of flags alone. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

2.2 **Local three-case calculation in the corrected chart.** For a column $S$ write $n_S(a)=\mathbf1_{a\in S}$ and omit a replacement term if it would collide. The transported coproduct gives $E_aM_{L,R}=M_{L,R(a+1\mapsto a)}+s^{n_R(a)-n_R(a+1)}M_{L(a+1\mapsto a),R}$ and $F_aM_{L,R}=M_{L(a\mapsto a+1),R}+s^{-n_L(a)+n_L(a+1)}M_{L,R(a\mapsto a+1)}$. Match exclusive pairs by increasing positive distance, deleting matched endpoints, and call the resulting set $\Sigma_f^+$. Distinct pairs at the same distance cannot share an endpoint, so this prescription is unambiguous. Choose the smallest left value $b=a+1$ that is a matched endpoint. If $a$ is absent on the left, let $h$ lower this $b$ to $a$ and apply $F_a$. If $a$ is present on the left, it must also occur on the right: otherwise its distance to the right partner of $b$ would be smaller, forcing it to be a matched left endpoint contrary to the choice of $b$. In this case let $h$ raise that right $a$ to $b$ and apply $E_a$. The matching rules then give three cases: when the lower left neighbor $a$ is shared, its pair endpoint in $h$ moves from $b$ to $a$ and all other pairs persist; when $a$ is absent on both sides the pair set persists with that endpoint lowered; when $a$ occurs only on the right, $h$ loses precisely the distance-one pair $(b,a)$. For every subset of the remaining pairs, the two displayed action formulas have coefficient one in the first two cases: if a selected pair moves the active letter to the other column, the two relevant occupation numbers agree. In the last case both columns of $h$ contain $a$ and neither contains $b$, so $F_aM_{h_\Sigma}=M_{f_\Sigma}+s^{-1}M_{f_{\Sigma\cup\{(b,a)\}}}$. No wedge sorting sign enters, since an adjacent integer replacement either preserves its sorted position or is zero on collision. [F4, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 **The opposite BGG coefficient identity.** From the tilting nature and maximal support of $X(B)$, every multiplicity can be computed as $(X(B):\Delta(A))=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(X(B),\nabla(A))$. Applying the exact contravariant $\Psi$ to the finite standard flag of $\bar P(B)$ reverses its order but preserves the multiplicities of its corresponding standard sections. Opposite BGG reciprocity therefore gives $(X(B):M(A))=(\bar P(B):\bar M(A))=[\bar M(A):\bar L(B)]$, the opposite parabolic composition coefficient. [F1, F2, step 2.1]

3.2 **Bar-fixed pair formula and coefficient.** The predecessor procedure in step 2.2 terminates: $\sum L-\sum R$ decreases by one at each predecessor, all entries remain in the finite interval between the original smallest and largest entries, and both column sizes are fixed. At its terminal tuple there is no positive exclusive pair; in the fixed union/intersection fiber this is the unique minimal label, so its monomial is fixed by the triangular bar of [F4]. Apply the recorded $E_a,F_a$ in reverse predecessor order; they are bar-fixed. The subset calculation of step 2.2 proves inductively that the resulting bar-fixed vector is $U_f=\sum_{\Sigma\subseteq\Sigma_f^+}s^{-|\Sigma|}M_{f_\Sigma}$. The empty subset gives $M_f$, every nonempty subset gives a lower label, and disjoint exclusive endpoints make distinct subsets give distinct tableaux. Thus $U_f$ has precisely the negative-chart triangular condition of $T_f$, and uniqueness in [F4] gives $U_f=T_f$. In particular every single greedy-pair coefficient is $s^{-1}$ and specializes to $1$. This supplies the local proof in the correct chart; it does not identify a positive-$s$ fixed vector with the negative-chart canonical family. [F4, step 1.2, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 **The tensor/wedge bridge to the source $T$ at $1$.** Writing each sorted entry tuple as a right coset representative $w_A$ (shortest right in the entry stabilizer) with $d(A)=w_A^{-1}$ shortest left, the pure tensor Hecke generator action and the reverse-position complementary-chart pairing identify the tensor coefficient matrix with the spherical values $P_{d(C)w_0,d(A)w_0}(1)$, i.e. with the ordinary singular multiplicities of [F3]; finite Levi Weyl cancellation turns the signed column-permutation expansion into the actual parabolic composition matrix, and the source-positive wedge embedding identifies the source $L$-vectors with the tensor $L$-vectors by ordinary-bar and triangular uniqueness. Applying the same argument in reverse columns and using the typed pairing $C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB}$ of [F4] identifies the coefficient of $M(A)$ in the source canonical vector $T_B$ at $1$ with the opposite BGG coefficient of step 3.1. [F2, F3, F4, step 3.1]


4.2 **Isolation of adjacent columns in a larger tensor.** If two tableaux have the same entries outside two adjacent columns, every tableau in the Bruhat interval between them has the same outer prefix weights, since dominance is antisymmetric on fixed total weight; parenthesizing the pair as one tensor factor, a positive transfer across an outer boundary strictly changes a prefix weight in the positive cone and cannot be cancelled by further positive transfers. Hence the bar submatrix and, by triangular correction, the canonical coefficient between the two labelled monomials equal the two-column values of step 3.2. [F1, F4, step 3.2]

5.1 **Genuine edges at $1$.** Specializing step 4.2 at $s=1$, a greedy-pair swap gives $(X(B):M(A))=1$ for the two labels connected by the swap: the corresponding standard factor occurs with multiplicity $1$ in the indecomposable tilting object $X(B)$. Since an indecomposable finite-length object cannot have composition factors in two different linkage blocks, and $M(A)$ has simple head $L(A)$ while the actual $\Delta(B)$ section of $X(B)$ supplies $L(B)$ as a composition factor, the labels $A$ and $B$ lie in the same actual linkage block. Opposite BGG gives $[\bar M(A):\bar L(B)]=1$, and $\bar M(A)$ has head $\bar L(A)$, so the same edge connects the opposite labels. [F1, F2, step 3.1, step 4.2]

6.1 **Connectivity of the binary tableau fiber.** Identify a tableau with the $0/1$ incidence matrix recording which entry values occur in each column; its row margins are entry multiplicities and its column margins are the heights $n_j$. The symmetric difference of two matrices with the same margins is a union of alternating cycles in the bipartite graph, and a cycle of length $2k$ is flipped by a chord: if the chord entry is $0$ flip the smaller four-cycle first and then the remaining shorter cycle, if it is $1$ flip the complementary shorter cycle first and then the four-cycle; the chord is restored and exactly the original cycle is flipped. Induction on the cycle length gives a sequence of valid $2\times2$ switches connecting any two matrices with the same margins. [step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 **Reduction of distant switches.** Reduce a switch of entries $a,b$ between nonadjacent columns $S,U$ through the next intermediate column $T$. If $T$ contains only $a$ or only $b$, two switches with shorter column distance restore $T$ and effect the $S/U$ switch. If $T$ contains both, then $T\setminus S$ contains $b$ and, since $|S|\ge|T|$, some $c\in S\setminus T$ with $c\ne a$; use $c\leftrightarrow b$ on $S,T$, then $a\leftrightarrow b$ on $T,U$, then $a\leftrightarrow c$ on $S,T$. If $T$ contains neither, then $U\setminus T$ contains $b$ and, since $|T|\ge|U|$, some $c\in T\setminus U$; use $c\leftrightarrow b$ on $T,U$, then $a\leftrightarrow b$ on $S,T$, then $a\leftrightarrow c$ on $T,U$. Every step is a valid binary switch preserving the margins, and induction on the column distance reduces to adjacent columns. These cardinal comparisons use exactly the original sorted heights $n_1\ge\cdots\ge n_l$. [step 6.1, algebra]

8.1 **Adjacent fibers connect through coefficient-$1$ edges.** Every adjacent two-column switch has both endpoints in one union/intersection fiber of the pair of columns. Repeatedly swapping any greedy positive pair strictly lowers the inversion order of the tuple, and the process terminates at the unique configuration in which all left-exclusive values precede all right-exclusive values. Hence the endpoints are connected through the canonical coefficient-$1$ edges of step 3.2 and step 5.1. [step 3.2, step 5.1, step 7.1]

9.1 **Conclusion.** Combining binary-fiber connectivity, distant-switch reduction and adjacent coefficient edges, the whole fixed-margin binary tableau fiber is connected through actual linkage edges, in the original central summand and, by step 5.1, in the opposite one. Hence both genuine type-$A$ tableau central summands are single linkage blocks, including repeated-entry singular ambient characters; no future higher-Schur/cyclotomic-centre theorem and no bare Bruhat-cover connectivity assertion is used. [step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, step 8.1] ∎

items.title: Standard tableau monomials form a basis of the highest weight Fock submodule
items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked based/global lattice suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], with source
parameter $s$, monomial basis $M_A$, ordinary bar $\psi$, source
dual-canonical family $L_A$, canonical family $T_A$, and the source forms
$\langle-,-\rangle$, $C$.

The highest vector $M_{A_\Lambda}$ generates the multiplicity-one constituent
$V(\Lambda)\subseteq F(\Lambda)$, and there is its normalized module projection
$\pi:F(\Lambda)\to V(\Lambda)$.

(1) The vectors $S_A:=\pi M_A$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a basis of
$V(\Lambda)$, and $D_A:=\pi L_A$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ form the
**source dual-canonical basis** of $V(\Lambda)$.

(2) What vanishes is $\pi L_A$ for $A$ not standard; $\pi M_A$ need not vanish
for nonstandard $A$. The integral kernel of $\pi$ is the saturated direct
summand with basis the $L_A$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and
$\pi(F_{\mathcal A})$ has the actual basis $D_A$ (also $S_A$ on
$\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$), the source upper/costandard lattice. For every $B$,
$$\pi M_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(s)\,D_A,$$
which gives the explicit straightening of nonstandard projected monomials.

(3) All bases and maps commute with upper cuts and common-tail embeddings, so
the assertions hold in the full direct limit. The relation of the source
$D_A$ to the library form-dual upper family
([[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]]) is the explicit weight
rescaling proved in the global-basis comparison, not an unqualified
identification.
items.strategy:
**Given:** Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] as specified above.  A finite cut of $F(\Lambda)$ with its monomial basis, ordinary bar $\psi$, source families $L,T$, forms $\langle-,-\rangle$, $C$, the highest constituent $V(\Lambda)$ with its normalized highest vector $M_{A_\Lambda}$, and the library based-module machinery.

[F1] Fock bases and forms ([[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], [[thm-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module-has-the-column-monomial-basis]], [[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]): monomial basis and its weights; triangular charts $d,p$; $C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}$, $C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB}$, $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$; rectification identifies $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$ with $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; cuts commute with all four families.

[F2] Based modules and global bases ([[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]], [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]], [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[thm-quasi-r-tensor-bars-on-finite-products-of-based-integrable-modules]], [[thm-crystal-bases-of-integrable-modules-decompose-into-highest-weight-crystals]], [[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]], [[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]): the normalized integrable highest module is ordinary simple and maps universally to an integrable cyclic highest module; finite tensor charts have the stated crystal rule; the contravariant form and its normalized highest constituent; existence, bar invariance and uniqueness of the lower global basis; bar lattices and crystal lattices.

[F3] Conventions ([[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]): source/library parameter dictionary, divided powers, bars and lattices.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The normalized highest inclusion.** The explicitly constructed fundamental factors make the ground tensor integrable and give it the unique top weight $\Lambda$. The universal highest-module map from the actual existence-and-uniqueness theorem sends the normalized highest vector to this ground tensor and has nonzero image. Ordinary simplicity of that highest module makes the map $j:V(\Lambda)\to F(\Lambda)$ injective. A module injection preserves each highest kernel and the unique divided-string decomposition, hence commutes with the intrinsic lower string shifts. It also sends divided-power generators to the actual integral tensor lattice. The normalized projection will be constructed by the finite nondegenerate pairing below, rather than assumed from a general semisimplicity assertion. Its uniqueness follows from the one-dimensional top weight: a nonzero map to the simple highest module is surjective, hence cannot vanish on the top weight. [F1, F2, F3, construct]

2.1 **The actual balanced tensor chart.** Let $L_0^{\rm ten}$ and $\Psi L_0^{\rm ten}$ be the actual two charts of the finite-product theorem, not the raw tensor-word chart. The normalized ground tensor is a nonzero ground crystal residue. Every generator of $L_0(\Lambda)$ is a divided-string word on its highest vector; the naturality established in step 1.1 and the actual tensor crystal rule put its image in $L_0^{\rm ten}$ with the corresponding nonzero ground-component residue, with nonvanishing ensured by the partial-inverse rule. Divided-power generation gives $jV_{\mathcal A}(\Lambda)\subseteq F_{\mathcal A}$. Both bar composites agree on the highest vector and on every bar-fixed divided lowering monomial, so $j\overline{L_0(\Lambda)}\subseteq\Psi L_0^{\rm ten}$. Hence $jG(b)$ is integral, lies in both actual charts, is bar fixed and has the required residue. Balanced uniqueness identifies it with the corrected tensor global vector. Since $t=s^{-1}$, this library zero chart is the source infinity chart: the original factor order yields $T_A$ on $\mathrm{Rev}$, and the reverse-factor order yields $\widetilde T_A$ on $\mathrm{Std}$. This proves based inclusion rather than assuming every module map is based. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 **The ground components.** On a strict column the crystal signature rule has $+$ for entry $i$ and $-$ for entry $i+1$ with simultaneous occurrences cancelling; concatenating down-column words, cancelling $-+$ pairs, the rightmost surviving $+$ and leftmost surviving $-$ determine the source upper operators. Semistandard rows are stable under this rule: a changed entry violating a row inequality has an equal neighbouring entry which is either a later surviving $+$, an earlier surviving $-$ or its cancelling mate, and column strictness forces the last matching in the same row strip. The only highest tableau of the closed set is the ground state: the rightmost column is consecutive ground, and inducting to the left, rows overlapping the already-ground right columns are forced to be ground while a gap above the overlap produces an unmatched minus; repeated raising decreases the sum of entries, bounded below on a finite interval. Thus the reverse-factor lower ground component, equivalently the source original-order upper signature component, is exactly $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; the original-order lower component is the reverse-standard set from step 2.1. [F1, F2, step 2.1]

4.1 **Rectification.** Reversing the tensor order gives the reverse reading of the same signature rule; aligning column tops by the prescribed vertical shifts makes the reverse-standard inequalities stable, and the explicit row-insertion rectification (bumping the smallest larger letter, with the elementary Knuth interchanges preserving the cancelling signs) is a weight-preserving crystal isomorphism between the original lower ground component and the reverse-factor lower ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, with inverse reverse insertion. This is the label dictionary of [F1]. [F1, step 3.1]

5.1 **The projection.** Define $\pi$ by $C_0(v,\pi y)=C(j_{\mathrm{reverse}}v,y)$, where $j_{\mathrm{reverse}}$ is the based reverse-factor highest inclusion. The required highest form is constructed from the actual library polarization $B_8$: at weight $\Lambda-\alpha$ put $C_0=s^{a(\alpha)}B_8$, $a(\alpha)=(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)/2$. Its nondegeneracy and highest value one follow from $B_8$. The translated adjoint is $\sigma(F_i)=sK_i^{-1}E_i$, $K_i=D_iD_{i+1}^{-1}$. For input weight $\mu$ this contributes $s^{1-\mu(h_i)}$, canceled by $a(\alpha+\alpha_i)-a(\alpha)=\mu(h_i)-1$. Thus $C_0(F_ix,y)=C_0(x,E_i y)$, and similarly $C_0(E_ix,y)=C_0(x,F_i y)$; toral operators remain self-adjoint. This constructs, rather than assumes, the normalized nondegenerate $\mathcal E\mathcal F$-contravariant form. Here is the needed typed contravariance locally. Let $B_0$ be the coefficient dot pairing of reversed and original tensor words, and write $\Psi=\Theta\overline{(\cdot)}_0$ on a finite product, with $\overline{(\cdot)}_0$ the factorwise coefficient bar. Since $\Psi M_B=\Theta M_B$, the normalization $C(\widetilde M_A,\Psi M_B)=\delta_{AB}$ gives $C(x,y)=B_0(x,\Theta^{-1}y)$. On each minuscule factor the matrices of $E_i$ and $F_i$ are transposes. Reversing the factors in the explicit coproduct therefore gives $B_0(E_i x,z)=B_0(x,\overline\Delta(F_i)z)$, $B_0(F_i x,z)=B_0(x,\overline\Delta(E_i)z)$, while toral $D_a$ is self-adjoint. The finite quasi-$R$ intertwiner satisfies $\Theta\overline\Delta(u)=\Delta(\overline u)\Theta$; for $E_i,F_i$ their bars equal themselves. Substitution proves $C(E_i x,y)=C(x,F_i y)$, $C(F_i x,y)=C(x,E_i y)$ and $C(D_a x,y)=C(x,D_a y)$, first on two factors and then by coproduct association on each finite product. The required complementary delta pairing can also be checked here. The paired-root Casimir terms of the finite quasi-$R$ expansion, under factor reversal and the minuscule $E/F$ transpose, give $\Theta_{\mathrm{reverse}}^{\mathsf T}=\overline\Theta^{-1}$; the inverse/factorization identities extend this from two factors to every finite product. Consequently $C$ commutes with both bars in the sense $C(\widetilde\Psi x,\Psi y)=\overline{C(x,y)}$. Since $L_B=\Theta\overline{L_B}_0$, one has $C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=B_0(\widetilde T_A,\overline{L_B}_0)$. The two coefficient families on the right have coefficients in $\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]$, with constant matrix the identity and every off-diagonal term in $s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]$. Their value is bar fixed by the preceding identity, hence belongs to $\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]\cap\mathbb Z[s]=\mathbb Z$, forcing $C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}$. The triangular bar-fixed families used here are obtained locally in finite weight spaces: at each lower label, involutivity makes the residual coefficient $r(s)$ satisfy $r(s)+r(s^{-1})=0$; its positive-power part, or negative-power part, gives the unique required correction, and induction on the finite lower ideal constructs the complementary charts. Thus this use requires neither an unproved Gram identity nor a presumed based embedding. These identities are over $\mathbb Q(s)$; any stated complex coefficient conjugation is restored on scalar extension. Thus the normalized highest form $C_0$ has precisely the required $E/F$ adjunction and toral symmetry, and $\pi$ is $U$-linear; its highest coefficient is $1$, so its composite with the original highest inclusion is the identity on the simple highest module. It is therefore a genuine normalized projection, and its uniqueness is the top-weight argument of step 1.1. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 4.1]

6.1 **Vanishing and the dual-canonical basis.** Since $j_{\mathrm{reverse}}$ sends the lower global basis to $\widetilde T_A$ with $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, the delta pairing $C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}$ of [F1] gives $\pi L_B=0$ for $B\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, while for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ the vectors $D_A=\pi L_A$ form the $C_0$-dual basis of the constituent. This proves the vanishing statement (2) and that the $D_A$ are the source dual-canonical basis. [F1, step 4.1, step 5.1]

7.1 **Straightening and the $S$-basis.** Expanding $M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}(s)L_A$ by the triangular chart of [F1] and applying $\pi$ gives $\pi M_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(s)\,D_A,$ the restriction to $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ of a unitriangular matrix with diagonal $1$; hence the projected monomials $S_A=\pi M_A$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a basis of the constituent and the displayed formula is the explicit straightening of every projected monomial, standard or not. No projected-monomial vanishing is claimed. [F1, step 6.1, algebra]

8.1 **The integral kernel and the source upper lattice.** By step 6.1 the kernel of $\pi$ is spanned by the $L_A$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; being spanned by a subset of a basis it is a saturated direct summand of the integral Fock lattice. The image $\pi(F_{\mathcal A})$ is spanned by the $D_A$, hence is the source upper/costandard lattice; it is not identified with the lower divided-power lattice by an $A$-unit Gram determinant, since the relevant monomial Gram matrices are the inverse ordinary-bar matrix rather than the identity. [F1, step 6.1, step 7.1]

9.1 **Cuts and the direct limit.** All constructions and all coefficients of steps 1.1-8.1 are stable under the upper-cut and common-tail embeddings by the declared truncation compatibility theorem, and every vector lies in some finite double cut; the normalized highest maps are unique, so the maps agree on overlaps. The compatible direct limit gives the full bounded or semi-infinite assertion, and the comparison with the library form-dual upper family is the explicit weight rescaling proved in the global-basis comparison. [F1, F2, step 3.1, step 8.1]

10.1 **Conclusion.** The highest Fock constituent $V(\Lambda)$ has the standard monomial basis $S_A$ and the source dual-canonical basis $D_A=[\pi L_A]$ over $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, with the explicit straightening formula and the saturated integral kernel off $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; the library comparison uses the weight rescaling only. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, step 8.1, step 9.1] ∎

items.title: The integral parabolic category-O blocks for higher-level Schur-Weyl duality
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and that $I$ is bounded
below, so $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are finite; the upper end of
$I$ may remain unbounded. Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n(\mathbb C)$ and let
the standard parabolic $\mathfrak p$ have Levi
$\mathfrak{gl}_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{n_l}$
([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]).
For a tableau $A$ let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ be its ordinary highest-weight
reading: read columns from left to right and each column from top to bottom,
so its entries are strictly decreasing. This is also the normally ordered column reading of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]. Put
$$\lambda_A=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(a_j+j-1)\,\varepsilon_j .$$
Strict columns make $\lambda_A$ Levi-dominant, so that the simple highest weight
module $L(A)$ of [[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]
and the induced generalized standard
$M(A)=M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda_A)$ of
[[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]] belong to the genuine
parabolic category $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ of
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]].

Use the published **half-sum convention**
$\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$; then
$$\lambda_{A,j}+\rho_j=a_j+\frac{n-1}{2},$$
so the $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ Harish-Chandra shifted-coordinate multiset of the
block is the tableau-entry multiset plus the common scalar $(n-1)/2$, and this
multiset together with the displayed scalar $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ centre labels the
central character ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]). The Fock
weight $\sum_j\delta_{a_j}=\Lambda-\alpha$ of the Fock item belongs to the
different $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ weight lattice and indexes that entry multiset;
it is **not** a literal $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ highest weight.

For an entry multiset $\alpha$ the corresponding **finite parabolic central
block** $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ has labels
$\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$, generalized standards $M(A)$, simples $L(A)$,
projective covers $P(A)$ and costandards $\nabla(A)$, with the BGG reciprocity,
restricted duality and highest-weight structure inherited from
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]; by
[[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]] it is a single
linkage block. Its simple and standard classes form bases of its Grothendieck
group, and its numerical multiplicities include repeated-entry singular central
characters. The direct sum over the admitted entry multisets is
$\mathcal O^\Lambda$. **Opposite blocks** use the reversed Levi order and the
reverse-column reading, with the correspondingly reversed label order
([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]).
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A bounded-below residue set $I$ with finite column heights $n_j$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$, the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ with standard parabolic of Levi $\mathfrak{gl}_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{n_l}$, the tableau readings $a_1,\dots,a_n$, the half-sum convention $\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$, and the Fock conventions of [[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]].

[F1] Parabolic category structure ([[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]], [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]], [[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]): generalized standards $M(A)$, simples, projectives, costandards, BGG reciprocity, restricted duality and finite highest-weight flags in each integral block.

[F2] Classical highest weights and characters ([[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]], [[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]], [[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]], [[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]], [[def-bgg-category-o]], [[def-verma-module]]): the finite Levi highest-weight classification, the dot-action and Harish-Chandra labelling of central characters, and character/Grothendieck bases.

[F3] Linkage ([[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]]): each of these genuine type-$A$ tableau central summands is a single linkage block, original and opposite.

[F4] Semi-regular duality ([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]): reversed Levi order, reverse-column reading and reversed label order.

[F5] Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Levi dominance and the shifted multiset.** Read each strict column from top to bottom, as stipulated for the ordinary highest-weight tuple. Then $a_j>a_{j+1}$ within each Levi block and the integral difference is at least one. Consequently $\lambda_{A,j}-\lambda_{A,j+1}=a_j-a_{j+1}-1\ge0$, so $\lambda_A$ is weakly dominant and integral for the Levi. Consecutive ground entries may give equality of these highest-weight coordinates, which is allowed. This ordinary tuple follows the same normally ordered column reading. Therefore $L(A)$ and $M(A)$ are genuine objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ by [F1]. Because $\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$ has total sum $0$, the $j$-th shifted coordinate is $\lambda_{A,j}+\rho_j=a_j+(n-1)/2$, so the shifted-coordinate multiset differs from the entry multiset by the common scalar $(n-1)/2$; by [F2] this multiset together with the trace-centre scalar determines the central character, with no undeclared full-staircase shift. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 **The block and its labels.** Fix an admitted entry multiset $\alpha$; its shifted-coordinate multiset gives one central character, and the simple modules $L(A)$ of that central character form exactly the labels $\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$ with $\mathrm{wt}(A)=\Lambda-\alpha$. The induced modules $M(A)$ are the generalized standards of the block, the projectives $P(A)$ and costandards $\nabla(A)$ exist by [F1], and BGG reciprocity and restricted duality hold blockwise because they are inherited from the ambient parabolic category. [F1, step 1.1]

3.1 **Filtered and Grothendieck structure.** By [F1] every object of the block has finite length with simple factors among the $L(A)$, and the projective covers have finite $M(A)$-flags; the simple and standard classes are bases of the block Grothendieck group with the stated unitriangular character matrix. By [F3] the block is a single linkage block, so all its labels are connected by actual indecomposable-tilting edges, including repeated-entry singular central characters; the direct sum over the admitted multisets is $\mathcal O^\Lambda$. [F1, F3, F5, step 2.1]

4.1 **Opposite blocks.** Reversing the Levi order and reading tableaux by columns in the reverse direction swaps the blocks and reverses the prefix order of the labels; by [F4] the reversed labels are the same tableaux with reversed column readings, and the corresponding central characters are the reversed-coordinate multisets. This is the opposite-block dictionary. [F3, F4, step 3.1] ∎

items.title: The residue translation functors on the sum of parabolic blocks
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and work with the finite
classical $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ tableau blocks of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]],
and with the general translation machinery of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]] and
[[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]].

Let $V$ be the natural $\mathfrak{gl}_n$-module and $V^{*}$ its dual. For a
residue $i$ define the **residue translation functor** $f_i$ on
$\mathcal O^\Lambda$ by tensoring with $V$ and projecting onto the entry-multiset
central character in which exactly one entry $i$ is replaced by $i+1$; define
$e_i$ by tensoring with $V^{*}$ and the reverse character change ($i+1\mapsto i$,
with the signs of the natural form). Concretely, on a block
$\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ the functor is the exact block projection
$\operatorname{pr}_{\alpha-\alpha_i}(-\otimes V)$ for $f_i$ and
$\operatorname{pr}_{\alpha+\alpha_i}(-\otimes V^{*})$ for $e_i$, where
$\alpha_i$ is the Fock root label of the dictionary item
([[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]).

On the direct sum $\mathcal O^\Lambda$ of the blocks these functors are exact
and biadjoint, preserve projective and injective objects, and commute with the
restricted transpose duality
([[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]]).
Equivalently, $f_i$ is the generalized $i$-eigencomponent of the tensor
Casimir (including the place factors), and $e_i$ is the generalized
$-n-i$-eigencomponent on the dual tensor product.

The functors are **special residue translations**, not automatically ordinary
regular-wall translations; the Fock root label shifts by $\pm\alpha_i$, and
that label is not the classical $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ highest weight.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The finite classical blocks $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ with their generalized standards, simples, projectives and costandards, the natural module $V$ and its dual $V^{*}$, a residue $i$, and the translation and block-projection machinery.

[F1] Translation and projection ([[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], [[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]], [[thm-category-o-decomposes-by-generalized-central-character]]): exactness and biadjunction of the finite tensor/block-projection functors, and the decomposition of $\mathcal O$ by generalized central characters.

[F2] Preservation of (co)projectives ([[lem-tensoring-a-projective-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-is-projective]], [[lem-block-projection-preserves-projectives]]): tensoring a projective with a finite-dimensional module is projective, and block projection preserves projectives; dually for injectives.

[F3] Duality ([[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]]): restricted duality is an exact contravariant involution fixing the finite natural modules with their forms and preserving blocks.

[F4] Block dictionary ([[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]): the central characters are labelled by entry multisets and the Fock root label $\alpha_i$ shifts one entry.

[F5] Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

## Verification

1.1 **Definition of the functors.** Tensoring with the finite-dimensional module $V$ preserves the ambient category $\mathcal O$, and the decomposition of $\mathcal O$ into generalized central characters [F1] provides the exact projection onto each character; the character shifts by replacing one entry $i$ with $i+1$ by the weight computation of [F4]. Hence $f_i=\operatorname{pr}\circ(-\otimes V)$ is a well-defined exact functor between the stated blocks, and $e_i$ is defined verbatim with $V^{*}$ and the reverse shift. [F1, F4, construct]

2.1 **Exactness and biadjunction.** On the direct sum of blocks, exactness is inherited from the exactness of tensoring with a finite-dimensional module and of the block projections [F1]. Biadjunction holds because the general clause of the published translation supplier applies to the finite modules $V$ and $V^{*}$ without any regular-wall crossing: the unit and counit are those of the tensor/block-projection adjunction, and they restrict to the stated blocks by construction of the projections. [F1, F5, step 1.1]

2.2 **The Casimir description.** On a weight vector of weight $\lambda$ in a block, the tensor Casimir of the natural factor acts by the scalar $\lambda_j+1-j$, i.e. by the entry $a_j$ of the tableau reading, and on the dual tensor product by $-a_j-n+1$; an entry $i+1$ therefore contributes the generalized eigenvalue $-n-i$. Hence the generalized $i$-eigencomponent of the tensor Casimir is exactly the functor $f_i$ of step 1.1, and the generalized $-n-i$-eigencomponent of the dual tensor product is $e_i$. This also identifies the Fock root labels: they shift by $\pm\alpha_i$ and are not the classical highest weights. [F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 **Projectives and injectives.** If $P$ is projective in a block, $P\otimes V$ is projective in $\mathcal O$ by [F2], and the block projection of a projective is projective by [F2]; hence $f_i$ and, dually, $e_i$ preserve projectives. Applying restricted duality [F3], which preserves the blocks and exchanges projectives with injectives, gives the injective statement. [F2, F3, step 2.1]

3.2 **Commutation with duality.** Restricted transpose duality fixes $V$ and $V^{*}$ with their respective forms and commutes with tensoring with a fixed finite-dimensional module and with the character projections; therefore $D f_i\cong f_i D$ and $D e_i\cong e_i D$ on the direct sum, which is the stated compatibility. [F3, step 2.1]

4.1 **Conclusion.** The residue translation functors $f_i,e_i$ on the direct sum of finite classical blocks are exact, biadjoint, preserve projectives and injectives, commute with restricted duality, and agree with the stated Casimir eigencomponents; they are special residue translations with the Fock root label shifts, not ordinary regular-wall translations and not classical highest-weight shifts. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 2.2] ∎

items.title: Parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials give the dual-canonical transition matrix

For $I$ bounded below use the actual finite classical tableau-block dictionary (including repeated entries). Fix the right place action $(a w)_i=a_{w(i)}$. Let $w_A$ be shortest with $a(A)w_A$ weakly increasing, and let $K$ be the Young stabilizer of that sorted multiset. Then $w_A$ is shortest RIGHT modulo $K$, $d(A)=w_A^{-1}$ shortest LEFT, and
$$p_{A,B}(s)=s^{\ell(w_B)-\ell(w_A)}\sum_{z\in K}(-1)^{\ell(z)}P_{w_Az,w_B}(s^{-2}).$$
This is the ANTISPHERICAL/sign family for the ENTRY stabilizer, in the left convention after inversion, with Hecke variable $v=s$; the library QUANTUM parameter is instead $t=s^{-1}$. It has support $A\le B$ and diagonal1; $d$ is its inverse coefficient matrix through $p(-s)$. The COLUMN Levi subgroup $J$ is generally different from $K$. Assuming AC, the genuine parabolic block composition matrix is
$$[M(B):L(A)]=d_{A,B}(1)=\sum_{C\sim_{\rm col}B}(-1)^{\ell(B,C)}P_{d(C)w_0,d(A)w_0}(1).$$
This uses singular ordinary SPHERICAL coefficients for the entry stabilizer inside finite Levi cancellation, so covers mixed singular-ambient/parabolic-Levi blocks. It does not identify a singular category with genuine parabolic O or identify the two polynomial families by an opposite convention.

items.title: Residue Casimir operators and local affine-Hecke actions
items.statement: Assume AC and work with finite $n$ classical $gl_n$ category O, distinct from the Fock algebra $gl_{I^+}$. Tensor Casimir $x_j$ on the jth natural factor (including all preceding factors) and adjacent place swaps $T_j$ on $M\otimes V^{\otimes r}$ satisfy the degenerate affine-Hecke relations: commuting $x_j$, symmetric-group braid/quadratic relations, $T_jx_j-x_{j+1}T_j=-1$ and commuting distant generators. They restrict naturally to repeated residue functors $f_i^r$, where $x_j-i$ is locally nilpotent; dual actions are biadjoint mates on $e_i^r$. Finite Levi tensor decomposition and exact PBW induction give multiplicity-free generalized-standard flags for the entry moves $i\to i+1$ and $i+1\to i$. The standard-class map $[\Delta(A)]\mapsto M_A$ gives the full integral Fock K0 action, its Chevalley/Serre relations and local integrability; each root's biadjoint functors therefore give a positive, locally finite $sl_2$ action on the simple-class basis. The ground-state class generates the highest constituent, not generally the entire tensor Fock module.
items.strategy: The natural tensor Casimir is sum E_ab tensor E_ba, and x_j adds the place transpositions with earlier natural factors. Matrix-unit multiplication proves x commutation and T_jx_jT_j=x_{j+1}−T_j, hence the listed relations, with braid and distant commutation immediate on places. For highest weight lambda_j=a_j+j−1, c(lambda)=sum lambda_j(lambda_j+n+1−2j), c(V)=n; the eigenvalue on the lambda+epsilon_j flag factor is (c(lambda+epsilon_j)−c(lambda)−n)/2=lambda_j+1−j=a_j. On lambda−epsilon_j in tensor V* it is −a_j−n+1; an entry i+1 therefore gives −n−i. Exact generalized eigenspaces select precisely the moves. Tensor identity plus finite Levi complete reducibility produces each valid column move once; projected invalid/repeated-column moves disappear. Standard and simple K0 bases and character injectivity were proved in15, so the standard-class map is an actual isomorphism and the induced generators are the explicit tensor/wedge action. Checking on this basis proves Chevalley and Serre relations, including the integral divided powers. Each residue root is locally finite because the fixed finite boxes have only two relevant entries and repeated replacements terminate. Biadjunction, finite length and positivity in the simple basis make class vanishing equivalent to functor vanishing, satisfying every weak-sl2 hypothesis without a forward reference to the later combined action theorem. Restrict x to the chosen generalized eigenfunctor; nilpotence follows on finite flags, hence on finite length. Define the dual x/T by mates, which preserves the relations and both adjunctions.

items.statement:
Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked based/global lattice suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]:
source parameter $s$, library parameter $t=s^{-1}$. On the highest constituent
$V(\Lambda)\subseteq F(\Lambda)$ put $a(\alpha)=(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)/2$ at
weight $\Lambda-\alpha$.

(1) Under the proved convention and pairing dictionary, the library lower
global vector is
$$G_{\mathrm{low}}(A)=T_{A^{\uparrow}}=s^{-a(\alpha)}P_A\qquad(A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda),$$
whereas the actual library form-dual upper vector is
$$G_{\mathrm{up}}(A)=s^{a(\alpha)}D_A,\qquad D_A=\pi L_A .$$
Source $D_A$ is ordinary-bar fixed; its rescaled library upper vector is fixed
by the form-adjoint upper bar, with the genuine dual integral lattices and
charts of [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]].

(2) The source upper/costandard image lattice with basis $D_A$ is identified
with the library form-dual upper lattice by the weightwise units $s^{a(\alpha)}$.
Separately, the source quasi-canonical lattice with basis $P_A$ on the highest
constituent is identified with the library lower divided-power lattice by the
units $s^{-a(\alpha)}$. The embedded upper and lower lattices remain distinct;
no Laurent-unit Gram determinant or unit rescaling between those two embedded
lattices is asserted. All comparisons are integral and compatible with finite
cuts and their direct limits, and then with the supplier's permitted
specializations.

No ordinary-bar fixedness is asserted for the unqualified library upper family.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The lower family and the pairing.** By [F1] the based highest inclusion identifies the corrected tensor family $T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ with the lower global basis on $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and the projection $\pi$ is its $C_0$-adjoint; hence $C_0(T_{A^{\uparrow}},D_B)=\delta_{AB}$. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 **The weight recursion $B_8=s^{-a}C_0$.** The generator identities of the dictionary determine the library contravariant form $B_8$ and the normalized source form $C_0$ compatibly; on weight $\Lambda-\alpha$ the semilinear normalization gives $B_8=s^{-a(\alpha)}C_0$. Indeed the dictionary sends the library $\sigma$ at $t=s^{-1}$ to the source anti-involution, whose action on a lowered vector of weight $\mu$ contributes $s^{-\langle\mu,h_i\rangle-1}$, and the exponent identity $a(\alpha)-a(\alpha-\alpha_i)=\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+1$ with highest normalization and induction on lowering monomials proves the equality on every weight space. [F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 **Identification of the upper family.** Applying step 1.2 to step 1.1 gives $B_8(T_{A^{\uparrow}},s^{a}D_B)=\delta_{AB}$; by the dual-family uniqueness in [F2], the vectors $G_{\mathrm{up}}(A)=s^{a}D_A$ are the actual library form-dual upper vectors, fixed by the form-adjoint upper bar with the genuine dual lattices and charts. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2]

3.1 **The quasi-canonical family on the constituent.** The source form satisfies $\langle x,y\rangle=s^{a}C_0(\psi x,y)$ on the constituent. To verify the actual recurrence, put $K_i=D_iD_{i+1}^{-1}$. The coefficient Gram formula $\Theta^{-1}$ and the minuscule generator transpose identities give $\langle E_i x,y\rangle=\langle x,sF_iK_i^{-1}y\rangle$, $\langle F_i x,y\rangle=\langle x,s^{-1}K_iE_i y\rangle$ and the toral adjoint $D_a^{-1}$; the finite coproduct intertwiner transports these identities through each tensor prefix. For example, on input weight $\mu$ the first adjoint has scalar $s^{1-\mu(h_i)}$. This is precisely the ratio $s^{a(\alpha)-a(\alpha+\alpha_i)}$, since $a(\alpha+\alpha_i)-a(\alpha)=\mu(h_i)-1$. Together with $C_0(E_ix,y)=C_0(x,F_iy)$, the ordinary bar and highest value one, induction on divided lowering monomials proves the displayed identity. These comparisons are made over $\mathbb Q(s)$, with the specified coefficient conjugation on complex scalar extension. The left annihilator of $\ker\pi$ under this form is $U$-stable by its anti-involution, contains the ground highest vector, and has dimension $\dim V(\Lambda)$; hence it is exactly the highest constituent. The delta evaluations of the quasi-canonical vectors show that $P_A$ lies in that annihilator for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; on the constituent the candidate $s^{a}T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ has the same delta evaluations against the $D$-basis by step 1.2 and annihilates the off-standard $L$-vectors by [F1], so whole-Fock dual uniqueness gives $P_A=s^{a}T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ on $V(\Lambda)$. [F1, F3, step 1.2, step 2.1]

4.1 **Integrality, cuts and limits.** The units $s^{\pm a(\alpha)}$ are Laurent monomials, so the $D$-to-library-upper and $P$-to-library-lower comparisons of steps 1.1-3.1 are separately weightwise integral; their charts are the corresponding actual rescaled or dual charts. This is not a comparison of the embedded upper and lower lattices with each other. The finite double-cut compatibility of the Fock bases and of the library global bases, together with uniqueness of the normalized highest maps, proves the full direct-limit statement, and only the actual integral and specialization clauses of [F4] are used. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1]

5.1 **Conclusion.** The library lower global vector is $G_{\mathrm{low}}(A)=s^{-a}P_A$, the actual form-dual upper vector is $G_{\mathrm{up}}(A)=s^{a}D_A$, and the source quasi-canonical family satisfies $P_A=s^{a}T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ on the highest constituent; the source $D$ image lattice compares with the library form-dual upper lattice by $s^a$, while the source $P$ lattice compares with the library lower divided-power lattice by $s^{-a}$; the embedded upper and lower lattices are kept distinct, and no ordinary-bar fixedness is claimed for the unqualified library upper family. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

items.title: The local affine-Hecke socle argument for residue translations
items.statement: Assume AC and the preceding positive biadjoint residue $sl_2$/local degenerate affine-Hecke action. At a coincident eigenvalue the completed affine-Hecke algebra on r steps is $Mat_{r!}$ over the completed symmetric polynomial centre. The first-i image in its central fibre is $Mat_{i!}(Z_{i,r})$, where $Z_{i,r}=\mathbb C[c_1,\ldots,c_i]/(h_{r-i+1},\ldots,h_r)$ is a finite local complete-intersection Frobenius ring of dimension $\binom ri$ and one-dimensional socle. Divided residue functors and the complementary-idempotent restriction have the corresponding simple head/socle. Consequently $e_iL(A)$ and $f_iL(A)$ are either0 or self-dual indecomposables with simple isomorphic head and socle labelled $\tilde e_iA$ and $\tilde f_iA$, respectively. Vanishing is exactly absence of that crystal edge. This retains the complete residue-translation crystal claim, not only its K0 action.
items.strategy: Use polynomial representation T_j=s_j−partial_j, partial_j=(1−s_j)/(x_j−x_{j+1}); PBW follows by ordered spanning and leading permutation independence after localization. At the coincident completion, partial_j=(x_j−x_{j+1}+1)^−1(1−T_j), with LEFT inverse. Polynomial multiplication and longest divided difference give the relative perfect trace; reduction is the actual coinvariant Frobenius pairing, and complete-local Nakayama gives every matrix unit. The trivial/sign symmetric-group idempotents have fibre rank1: divided-difference terms lower degree and the diagonal character is the regular coinvariant character; idempotent splitting and Nakayama lift rank1. Partial elimination of remaining elementary coefficients gives the displayed h-relations. Their only common zero is0, since vanishing of i consecutive h's and their recurrence makes the reciprocal elementary series polynomial, hence constant. Nullstellensatz makes the quotient finite; polynomial Cohen–Macaulayness and the actual system-of-parameters theorem give regularity, globally by homogeneous localization. Koszul Hilbert series yields dimension binomial(r,i); the variable and h Koszul resolutions compute a unique socle in degree i(r−i). Thus no Grassmannian/Poincare theorem is imported. The ordered partial ring is free of rank i! over this centre and has dimension r!/(r−i)!, by successive monic distinguished-root equations. PBW group cosets and this basis prove the restriction freeness; the complementary idempotent removes (r−i)! multiplicity and leaves the indecomposable projective over Mat_{i!}(Z), with simple head/socle. These are the full algebraic steps of CR3.2–3.3/3.6. In the positive simple-class basis the sl2 string-height filtration is stable; biadjunction prevents a socle/head summand of E^jS from having lower maximal string height than S. At an extremal simple FS=0, E^(r)S is a single opposite-extremal simple by finite sl2 string theory/positivity. The Hecke action on E^rS has multiplicity module K_r; complementary restriction forces the socle/head of E^(j)S simple, since no maximal-height summand is killed by E^(r−j). Dimension comparison gives binomial(r,j) leading multiplicity and smaller-height other factors. For a general S take an extremal quotient of F^(h_minus)S and use adjunction to embed S in its divided translate; the opposite extremal translate is a sum of one simple, and the adjoint Hom into its simple socle bounds its multiplicity by1. This proves CR5.20 without importing it as a black box. Source Fock L is the balanced SOURCE upper-chart family. Kashiwara93§5.1 proves kernels of powers spanned by the global vectors with bounded epsilon (apply the maximal string power and balanced injectivity); §5.2 finite sl2 highest-string filtration is balanced by isolating a maximal constituent and annihilator test, whose remainder lies in the zero triple intersection. Thus in each associated string fG=[phi]G(tilde f) and eG=[epsilon]G(tilde e), and all other constituents have smaller corresponding height. The actual upper/lower string definitions in§3, the two source-positive coefficient charts and the typed reverse pairing verify these hypotheses; this is not the library8 adjoint-bar family by fiat. The full source5.3.1 proof uses the upper divided-string expansion and kernel-spanning induction to lift that leading term. At1, comparing with the preceding categorical unique maximal-height factors gives precisely the stated tableau labels. Commuting restricted duality makes head and socle equal and gives self-duality; one simple socle forces indecomposability.

items.statement: Assume AC. items.title: Indecomposable tilting objects exist and are classified in parabolic category O
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Every label $A$ in a
genuine tableau parabolic block of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
has a unique indecomposable tilting object $T(A)$ whose standard flag begins
with $M(A)$ once at the bottom and has all remaining labels $B<A$.
Equivalently, $T(A)$ has that maximal-label normalized standard flag and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1(M(B),T(A))=0$ for all $B$. Every tilting object is a finite
direct sum of these, and their classes form a unitriangular Grothendieck basis.
Restricted duality fixes $T(A)$. For a finite lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing
$A$ the corresponding partial tilting is the same ambient $T(A)$, since all
support labels are $\le A$; compatible ideal systems therefore stabilize in each
finite block, with flag-preserving inclusions. No uniqueness is claimed from a
bottom-standard occurrence alone without indecomposability and maximal support.
In the inline prinjectivity claim, $P(A)$ is projective-injective (equivalently
self-dual) exactly when $A$ is standard; in that case $P(A)=T(A^{\uparrow})$
with the proved rectification label.
