## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A finite genuine tableau parabolic block with its generalized standards $M(A)$, simples $L(A)$, projectives $P(A)$ and the filtered category of [[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]]; the semi-regular duality $\Psi$ and $F=D\Psi$ of [[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]; the residue functors and their head/socle behavior of [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]]; the highest-component normalization of [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]; the standard-monomial basis of [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]].

[F1] Filtered categories ([[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]]): the homological criterion, uniqueness of an indecomposable tilting object with bottom label $A$ and maximal support, BGG reciprocity, restricted duality, closure under summands and lower-ideal invariance.

[F2] Semi-regular duality ([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]): $\Psi$ is an exact contravariant equivalence of opposite and target standard-flag categories, sends $\bar\Delta(A)$ to $\Delta(A)$, and reverses the label order; $D\Psi$ is covariant and takes opposite standards to target costandards.

[F3] Parabolic structure ([[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]], [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]], [[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]], [[cor-injectives-have-costandard-filtrations]], [[lem-finite-length-objects-decompose-into-indecomposables]], [[prop-projective-covers-in-o-are-indecomposable-and-unique]], [[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]): enough projectives and injectives, finite-length decomposition, uniqueness of projective covers, generalized-standard flags.

[F4] Residue functors and labels ([[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]], [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]): simple head/socle of residue translates, the projection kernel spanned by off-standard $L$-vectors, the straightening formula, and the normalization $P_A=s^{a}T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ at $s=1$.

[F5] Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Construction from actual exact sequences.** Let $\bar P(A)$ be the labelled opposite projective cover. Its highest-weight sequence is $0\to\bar K(A)\to\bar P(A)\to\bar\Delta(A)\to0$, with $\bar K(A)$ standard-filtered by labels strictly above $A$. Applying $\Psi$ gives $0\to M(A)\to X(A)\to\Psi\bar K(A)\to0$, where $X(A)=\Psi\bar P(A)$ and the quotient has a finite standard flag with labels strictly below $A$. Its endomorphism algebra is the opposite of the local endomorphism algebra of $\bar P(A)$, so $X(A)$ is indecomposable. For an arbitrary extension $0\to X(A)\to Z\to M(B)\to0$, extension closure makes $Z$ standard-filtered. Inverting $\Psi$ turns this into an extension with source projective $\bar P(A)$ as quotient, which splits; exact equivalence transfers the splitting back. Hence $\operatorname{Ext}^1(M(B),X(A))=0$ for every $B$. The proved homological criterion of [F1] gives a costandard flag of $X(A)$, so it is the required actual tilting object with normalized bottom-standard inclusion. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 **Uniqueness.** Let $T,T'$ be two indecomposable tilting objects with $M(A)$ once at the bottom and all other labels $\prec A$. Extending the common normalized bottom inclusion both ways uses $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ vanishing against standard flags, and the resulting composites restrict to the identity on the bottom standard, hence are not nilpotent; finite-dimensional local $\operatorname{End}$ and Fitting's lemma force them to be isomorphisms. So $T\cong T'$, and [F1] identifies its unique maximal support label as $A$. [F1, step 1.1]

3.1 **Every tilting is a sum of these.** Let $T\ne0$ be an arbitrary tilting object and let $\Gamma$ be the lower ideal generated by its entire composition support. Choose one maximal support label $A$, which is maximal in $\Gamma$, and put $m=[T:L(A)]\ge1$. All standard and costandard sections of $T$ have labels in $\Gamma$, so it is tilting in that truncated highest-weight category. The proved maximal-standard trace in [F1] injects $\Delta(A)^{\oplus m}$ into $T$ with standard-filtered quotient. Choose one copy $i:\Delta(A)\hookrightarrow T$; its quotient is still standard-filtered, since the other $m-1$ copies and the trace quotient have such flags. Let $j:\Delta(A)\hookrightarrow X(A)$ be the actual normalized inclusion of step 1.1. Since $X(A)/\Delta(A)$ is standard-filtered and $T$ is tilting, $\operatorname{Ext}^1(X(A)/\Delta(A),T)=0$ extends $i$ to $f:X(A)\to T$ with $fj=i$. Similarly $\operatorname{Ext}^1(T/\Delta(A),X(A))=0$ extends $j$ to $g:T\to X(A)$ with $gi=j$. The composite $gf$ fixes the nonzero bottom standard of the indecomposable $X(A)$, so it is invertible by the finite local-End/Fitting argument. Hence $f$ splits with retraction $(gf)^{-1}g$, and $T\cong X(A)\oplus T'$. The complement is tilting by summand closure and has strictly smaller length; induction proves the stated finite decomposition. Incomparable maximal support labels and multiplicities $m>1$ are both allowed: no normalized flag of the entire $T$ was assumed. [F1, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 **Duality, ideals and Grothendieck basis.** Restricted duality makes $DT(A)$ an indecomposable tilting object with the same composition support $\le A$ and $[DT(A):L(A)]=1$. In the lower highest-weight ideal of labels $\le A$, the maximal-standard trace proved in [F1] gives an inclusion $M(A)\hookrightarrow DT(A)$ with standard-filtered quotient of strictly smaller labels, since its multiplicity space has dimension one. This supplies an actual normalized standard flag, so uniqueness identifies $DT(A)\cong T(A)$. If $\Gamma$ is a lower ideal containing $A$, every support label of $T(A)$ lies in $\Gamma$, so $T(A)$ computed in the ambient block lies in the Serre subcategory of $\Gamma$ and coincides with the partial tilting there; the classes $[T(A)]$ are unitriangular in the standard basis by the flag multiplicities, hence form a Grothendieck basis. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 **The projection kernel and standard embeddings.** The projection $\pi$ of [F4] has kernel spanned by the $L$-vectors off $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and is $U$-stable; the residue functors have nonnegative composition coefficients, so iterating them on an off-standard simple never produces a standard composition factor. Every generalized standard $M(B)$ embeds into an iterated $e$-word applied to an irreducible standard $M(C)$: add successively huge offsets to the later columns so that all later entries lie above the earlier ones, making $C$ the unique minimum in its fixed-multiset tableau order and hence $M(C)=L(C)$ simple; then lower the later-column entries back, column by column and bottom to top, with the explicit residue word. A later column stays above the active residues, so a wrong move can only occur in an earlier column and strictly increases an earlier prefix weight; hence $B$ is the unique maximal final standard section and occurs once, and the canonical maximal trace embeds $M(B)$ at the bottom. If $L(A)$ embedded into $M(B)$ with $A$ off standard, adjunction would give the standard $L(C)$ as a quotient of an $f$-word applied to $L(A)$, impossible by kernel stability. [F4, step 3.1]

5.1 **Converse and prinjectivity.** Conversely every standard label is reached from the ground simple projective by the crystal $f$-word, and the simple-head clause of [F4] makes $P(A)$ a summand of that translated projective-injective, hence injective; projectivity of $P(A)$ is by definition. A projective-injective indecomposable is self-dual: $DP(A)=P(B)$ with $[P(A)]=[P(B)]$ because simple classes are duality-fixed and the Cartan matrix is $DD^{t}$ with unitriangular invertible $D$, so $A=B$. A self-dual $P(A)$ has its head in its socle, and its standard flag embeds that simple into a standard section; conversely if $A$ is standard then $P(A)$ is projective-injective by the previous sentence. BGG reciprocity and [[thm-parabolic-kl-polynomials-give-the-dual-canonical-transition-matrix]] identify the standard coefficients of $[P(A)]$ with the transpose composition matrix defining the quasi-canonical vector $P_A$ at $s=1$. Thus the normalization $P_A=s^{a}T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ of [F4] identifies that actual projective class with the source canonical vector at $s=1$, whose unitriangular monomial expansion has unique maximal label $A^{\uparrow}$. Since $P(A)$ is an indecomposable tilting object its unique maximal standard label identifies it as $T(A^{\uparrow})$. [F3, F4, step 4.1]

6.1 **Conclusion.** Every label has a unique normalized indecomposable tilting object with the stated maximal-support flag, every tilting is a finite sum of these, restricted duality fixes them, lower ideals stabilize the same objects, and $P(A)$ is projective-injective exactly for standard $A$, in which case $P(A)=T(A^{\uparrow})$; no Irving criterion or future Schur-theoretic input is used. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, step 5.1] ∎

items.title: The Ringel dual of a finite highest weight ideal
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). In a finite
highest-weight block or in a lower Serre ideal $\Gamma$ of
[[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]]
put
$$T_\Gamma=\bigoplus_{A\in\Gamma}T(A),\qquad R_\Gamma=\operatorname{End}(T_\Gamma)^{\mathrm{op}},$$
the **characteristic tilting generator** and its opposite endomorphism ring.
By the classification theorem
([[thm-indecomposable-tiltings-exist-and-are-classified-in-parabolic-category-o]])
$T_\Gamma$ is Ext-self-orthogonal and has finite projective dimension.

The **Ringel-dual category** of $\Gamma$ is the category of finite-dimensional
left $R_\Gamma$-modules, made a highest-weight category by the reversed poset
and the standards
$$\Delta_R(A)=\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,\nabla(A)),\qquad A\in\Gamma .$$
The functor $\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,-)$ is exact and fully faithful on
costandard-filtered objects and identifies them with standard-filtered
Ringel-dual objects; projectives of the dual category correspond to tilting
objects of the original. Its algebraic realization by the opposite-parabolic
highest-weight quotient is proved in the next theorem.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A finite highest-weight block or lower Serre ideal $\Gamma$ with its generalized standards $M(A)$, costandards $\nabla(A)$, tiltings $T(A)$ and filtered categories, as in [[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]] and [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].

[F1] Tilting and filtered structure ([[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]], [[thm-indecomposable-tiltings-exist-and-are-classified-in-parabolic-category-o]]): the homological criteria, the maximal-support normalization of the indecomposable tiltings $T(A)$, that every tilting is a finite sum of these, and closedness of the flag categories under extensions and summands.

[F2] Grothendieck and projective machinery ([[thm-finite-length-grothendieck-groups-have-simple-class-bases]], [[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]], [[def-projective-object]], [[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]], [[lem-finite-length-objects-decompose-into-indecomposables]]): finite-length decomposition, projective objects and standard flags of projectives.

[F3] Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **Ext-self-orthogonality and finite projective dimension.** Each $T(A)$ has a standard flag and each $T(B)$ has a costandard flag. All positive $\operatorname{Ext}$ groups between these two kinds of flags vanish by the locally proved criterion of [F1], giving $\operatorname{Ext}^i(T(A),T(B))=0$ for every $i>0$. The actual projective sequence onto each standard has a standard-filtered kernel with strictly higher labels; starting at maximal labels, where the standard is projective, downward induction on the finite poset gives finite projective dimension for every standard. Long exact sequences along a finite standard flag then give finite projective dimension for every $T(A)$ and their finite sum $T_\Gamma$. The second flag in the Ext argument is costandard, and no standard/standard Ext vanishing is assumed. [F1, F2, F3]

2.1 **Costandard presentations by tiltings.** Dual to the normalized standard inclusion $M(A)\hookrightarrow T(A)$, every costandard object admits a surjection from a tilting object with costandard-filtered kernel; induction on the costandard flag length gives such presentations for every costandard-filtered object. [F1, step 1.1]

3.1 **Exactness and full faithfulness of $\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,-)$.** On costandard flags the functor sends the presentations of step 2.1 to projective presentations of the images; two tilting presentations lift every map and identify its kernel, so the functor is exact on costandard-filtered objects and fully faithful. It sends tilting objects to projective objects because $\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,T(A))$ is a direct summand of the regular module. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 **The highest-weight structure of the dual.** The quotient $\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,T(A))\to\Delta_R(A)=\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,\nabla(A))$ has a kernel filtered by standards with labels strictly higher in the reversed order, and its endomorphism ring is $\mathbb C$ with head labelled $A$; this follows from full faithfulness in step 3.1 and the maximal tilting support of [F1]. Hence the Ringel-dual category is highest weight with the reversed poset and the displayed standards, and its filtered image is $\mathcal F(\Delta_R)$, not $\mathcal F(\nabla_R)$. [F1, step 3.1]

5.1 **Conclusion.** $T_\Gamma$ is a characteristic tilting generator with Ext-self-orthogonal summands and finite projective dimension, the Ringel-dual category has the reversed poset with standards $\Delta_R(A)=\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,\nabla(A))$, and $\operatorname{Hom}(T_\Gamma,-)$ is an exact fully faithful equivalence from costandard-filtered objects to standard-filtered dual objects, exchanging tiltings with projectives; the algebraic realization is proved in the next theorem. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

items.title: The parabolic category-O Grothendieck group is the integral Fock module
items.statement: Assume AC and $I$ bounded below. The standard-class map $[M(A)]\mapsto M_A$ identifies the direct-sum K0 of genuine tableau parabolic blocks with the full integral Fock module, with matching multiset degrees and residue Chevalley action of $gl_{I^+}$. For every projective $P$ and finite-length $N$, $\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)=\langle[P],[N]\rangle$ at $s=1$. In particular $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$; no false standard/simple orthogonality $\langle M_A,L_B\rangle=\delta$ is asserted. The projective, simple and tilting basis identifications are proved separately below.
items.strategy: Use the genuine finite-length simple/standard bases and Casimir standard-flag operator identification, then extend the degree-preserving standard-class map over the direct sum. Write D_{A,B}=[M(B):L(A)] with simple rows and standard columns. BGG gives [P(A):M(B)]=D_{A,B}; only simple-to-standard expansion uses D^-1. The actual finite-cut quasi-R root factors have nonconstant coefficients divisible by s-s^-1 and regular at s=1, so tensor bars and primitive wedge bar matrices specialize to the identity, as do their inverse monomial Gram matrices. The D projective expansion paired with the D^-1 simple expansion gives delta. Exact Hom(P,-) and composition-series additivity then give the general projective/module pairing. No graded category-O lift or standard/simple orthogonality is asserted.

items.title: Type-A parabolic category-O Ringel duality via the opposite parabolic
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the actual type-$A$
tableau parabolic data of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].
Let $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ have the reversed Levi block order, conjugate to the
opposite parabolic, with reverse-column labels, and let
$F=D\Psi$ be the exact **covariant** equivalence constructed by
[[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]].
Then
$$F:\mathcal F(\bar\Delta)\simeq\mathcal F(\nabla),\qquad F(\bar M(A))=\nabla(A),\qquad F(\bar P(A))=T(A),$$
and the explicit highest-weight shifts cancel to the original column reading, so
labels $A$ and the matching central-character blocks are preserved. Therefore the
full-block Ringel dual is the opposite-parabolic block, and
$$(T(A):M(B))=[\bar M(B):\bar L(A)] .$$
For a proper original lower ideal $\Gamma$, its Ringel dual is the matching
opposite **highest-weight Serre quotient** by the complementary labels (an upper
ideal in the opposite order), not the same Serre down-set subcategory. The
filtered equivalence and the projective/tilting corner construction give this
compatible finite-ideal transport. No unchanged underived full-longest Borel
twisting and no equivalence on arbitrary category-$\mathcal O$ objects is
asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The reversed-block parabolic $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ with its semi-regular bimodule and the covariant equivalence $F=D\Psi$ of [[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]; the tilting classification of [[thm-indecomposable-tiltings-exist-and-are-classified-in-parabolic-category-o]]; the Ringel-dual definition of [[def-the-ringel-dual-of-a-finite-highest-weight-ideal]]; the block structure of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]] and [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]].

[F1] Semi-regular duality ([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]): exactness on the finite flag categories, $F(\bar\Delta(A))=\nabla(A)$, preservation of central blocks, and the label map.

[F2] Tilting classification ([[thm-indecomposable-tiltings-exist-and-are-classified-in-parabolic-category-o]], [[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]]): uniqueness/maximal support, $T(A)$ with $M(A)$ once at the bottom, restricted duality fixing tiltings, and lower-ideal invariance.

[F3] Ringel duality ([[def-the-ringel-dual-of-a-finite-highest-weight-ideal]]): the characteristic tilting generator and the exact fully faithful Hom to the reversed highest-weight category.

[F4] BGG and duality ([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]], [[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]], [[def-projective-object]], [[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]]): opposite projective BGG reciprocity, self-duality of tiltings, and projective presentations.

[F5] Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The equivalence on flags and its variance.** By [F1] the functor $F=D\Psi$ is exact and covariant on the finite generalized-standard flag categories, sends $\bar M(A)$ to $\nabla(A)$, preserves the central blocks and maps the reverse-column labels to the original ones by the explicit offset computation; it is an equivalence onto the costandard-filtered objects. [F1]

2.1 **Actual projective-to-tilting transport.** Put $X(A)=\Psi(\bar P(A))$. In the source highest-weight block the labelled projective has an exact sequence $0\to\bar K(A)\to\bar P(A)\to\bar\Delta(A)\to0$, with $\bar K(A)$ standard-filtered by labels strictly above $A$. The exact contravariant equivalence $\Psi$ turns it into $0\to\Delta(A)\to X(A)\to\Psi\bar K(A)\to0$; the reversed label order makes the quotient standard-filtered by labels strictly below $A$. If $0\to X(A)\to Z\to\Delta(B)\to0$ is any extension in the target block, then $Z$ is standard-filtered. Applying the inverse of $\Psi$ gives a surjection onto the source projective $\bar P(A)$, so the transformed extension splits, and therefore the original one splits. Thus $\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta(B),X(A))=0$ for every $B$. The homological characterization in [F2] makes $X(A)$ a genuine tilting object. Its endomorphism ring is the opposite of the local ring $\operatorname{End}(\bar P(A))$, so it is indecomposable. Its actual bottom-standard sequence and uniqueness in [F2] give $X(A)\cong T(A)$. Finally $F(\bar P(A))=DX(A)\cong DT(A)\cong T(A)$. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 **Reciprocity.** The exact covariant functor $F$ takes the source standard flag to a target costandard flag, so $(T(A):\nabla(B))=(\bar P(A):\bar\Delta(B))=[\bar\Delta(B):\bar L(A)]$ by source BGG reciprocity. Since $DT(A)\cong T(A)$ and $D\Delta(B)=\nabla(B)$, its standard and costandard multiplicities agree. This proves $(T(A):M(B))=[\bar M(B):\bar L(A)]$. [F2, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 **Full blocks and proper ideals.** Since both filtered equivalences are fully faithful, the endomorphism ring of the opposite projective generator equals that of the characteristic tilting generator, so the full-block Ringel dual is the opposite-parabolic block. For a proper original lower ideal $\Gamma$, every $T(A)$ with $A\in\Gamma$ has support $\le A$ and remains unchanged in the Serre truncation; its end algebra equals that of the corresponding sum of opposite full projectives. The functor $\operatorname{Hom}$ from that sum is exact, kills precisely the complementary simples, and is dense by projective presentations, realizing the Serre quotient as the corner $e_\Gamma\bar Ae_\Gamma$; this is the opposite highest-weight quotient by the complementary labels, an upper ideal in the opposite order, not the same down-set subcategory. [F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1]

5.1 **Conclusion.** The covariant semi-regular equivalence identifies the opposite standard flags with target costandard flags, sends opposite projectives to tiltings, preserves labels and central blocks, gives the reciprocity $(T(A):M(B))=[\bar M(B):\bar L(A)]$, and realizes the Ringel dual of the full block as the opposite-parabolic block and of a proper lower ideal as the opposite highest-weight Serre quotient; no unchanged full-longest Borel twisting or arbitrary-object equivalence is asserted. items.statement: Assume AC and the genuine tableau K0/Fock identification at $s=1$. For every label A, $[L(A)]=L_A$, $[P(A)]=P_A$ and $[T(A)]=T_A$. The projective coefficients are $d_{A,B}(1)$ by BGG; tilting coefficients are the OPPOSITE/reverse-column composition coefficients $\widetilde d_{A,B}(1)$, by the exact parabolic Ringel equivalence. They are not generally the inverse-transpose of the ORIGINAL composition matrix. Simples, projectives and tiltings therefore give the dual-canonical, quasi-canonical and canonical Fock families, respectively. These are ungraded specializations; no Koszul grading or an identification of library upper/lower families is asserted.

items.title: The canonical and quasi-canonical bases need not coincide
items.statement:
In the four-dimensional model of
[[ex-four-fock-bases-in-a-small-two-factor-tensor-space]] the canonical and
quasi-canonical Fock families coincide on every label.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The rank-one Fock model with monomials $M_{00},M_{01},M_{10},M_{11}$, the source families $L,T,P$ of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], and the computed bar matrix and vectors of [[ex-four-fock-bases-in-a-small-two-factor-tensor-space]].

[F1] Bar and families ([[thm-the-qg-tensor-product-bar-is-triangular-and-compatible-with-fock-truncations]], [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]]): $\psi$ is triangular with $\psi M_{10}=M_{10}+(s^{-1}-s)M_{01}$ and fixes the other monomials; the canonical family is the $s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]$-chart and the quasi-canonical family is defined by the inverse transition matrix.

[F2] Highest constituent ([[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]], [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], [[ex-four-fock-bases-in-a-small-two-factor-tensor-space]]): the projection $\pi$, the rectified highest label $01^{\uparrow}=10$, and the rescaling $P_A=s^{a}T_{A^{\uparrow}}$ on the highest constituent with $a=1$.

## Counterexample

Take $I=\{0\}$, $I^+=\{0,1\}$, $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$, and retain the mixed order
$(M_{01},M_{10})$ and the notation of
[[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and
[[ex-four-fock-bases-in-a-small-two-factor-tensor-space]]. There
$$P_{01}=M_{01}+s\,M_{10}=s\,T_{10},$$
because $T_{10}=M_{10}+s^{-1}M_{01}$; but
$$P_{10}=M_{10}\neq M_{10}+s^{-1}M_{01}=T_{10}$$
over $\mathbb Q(s)$. Hence the canonical and quasi-canonical families are
different, and so are the dual-canonical and monomial families. The
highest-component label rectification is $01^{\uparrow}=10$ with
$a=1$, which exhibits the genuine power and label distinction: the coincidence
$P_{01}=sT_{10}$ happens on the rectified highest label, not by an identity of
the two index sets. At $s=1$ the highest-submodule vectors $P_{01}$ and $T_{10}$
agree after rectification, but the full canonical and quasi-canonical families
are still not interchangeable. This is no claim that every corresponding label
differs at $s=1$.

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The two families at label $10$.** In the mixed order the bar fixes $M_{01}$ and sends $M_{10}$ to $M_{10}+(s^{-1}-s)M_{01}$. A vector $M_{10}+cM_{01}$ is fixed exactly when $c-\bar c=s^{-1}-s$. The positive chart gives $c=-s$ and the negative chart gives $c=s^{-1}$; uniqueness follows because a bar-fixed polynomial in either $s\mathbb Z[s]$ or $s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]$ is zero. Thus $L_{01}=T_{01}=M_{01}$, $L_{10}=M_{10}-sM_{01}$ and $T_{10}=M_{10}+s^{-1}M_{01}$. Inverting the $L$ chart gives $M_{10}=L_{10}+sL_{01}$, so the transposed inverse chart is $P_{01}=M_{01}+sM_{10}$ and $P_{10}=M_{10}$. Linear independence of the two monomials proves $P_{10}\ne T_{10}$. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 **The rectified highest-label coincidence.** At label $01$ the same computations give $P_{01}=M_{01}+sM_{10}=sT_{10}$, so the two families do meet at the rectified highest label with the power $a=1$ of [F2]; this is an identity between specific vectors, not an identification of the two labelled families. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 **Conclusion.** Since $P_{10}\neq T_{10}$, the canonical and quasi-canonical families are different over $\mathbb Q(s)$; the dual-canonical and monomial families differ too, because $L_{10}=M_{10}-sM_{01}\neq M_{10}$. The highest-submodule coincidence $P_{01}=sT_{10}$ is exactly the rectified normalization of [F2], and at $s=1$ it does not make the whole families interchangeable. [step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

items.statement: Use classical $gl_3$, Levi(2,1), $I=\{0,1\}$ and $\Lambda=\Lambda_1+\Lambda_0$; take the distinct-entry regular block. In target tableau order let $A_0=(1,0|2)$, $A_1=(2,0|1)$, $A_2=(2,1|0)$, with highest weights $(1,1,4),(2,1,3),(2,2,2)$. The target standard/simple matrix is $D=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\0&1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Reverse readings $(2|1,0),(1|2,0),(0|2,1)$ give opposite highest weights $(2,2,2),(1,3,2),(0,3,3)$ and opposite matrix $N=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Verify the semiregular label shift, $F\bar M(A)=\nabla(A)$, $F\bar P(A)=T(A)$ and tilting-standard ROW matrix $N^t$, distinct from target projective-standard rows $D^t$. On the genuine target lower ideal $\Gamma=\{A_0,A_1\}$ the tilting rows are $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$; its Ringel dual is the opposite highest-weight SERRE QUOTIENT, with standard/simple rows $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Simples/canonical classes in the target ideal are unchanged ambient ones, whereas projective/quasi-canonical classes use the standard-flag truncation of the ambient projectives.
